generated_note: Values transcribed from retrieved FAO publications. See PARAMETERS.md for what is sourced, what is assumed, and what is still missing.

evidence.title: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56, Table 12: single crop coefficients Kc
limitations: Kc_mid is used as the whole-season coefficient; a single seasonal Kc cannot represent the initial and late stages
where the table prints a range, the midpoint is used and both bounds are recorded alongside it
the lower bound applies to sub-humid, low-wind conditions and the upper to arid, windy ones; the midpoint is not tuned to any district
not an agronomist review for any Indian district

evidence.title: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56, Table 22: maximum rooting depth and soil water depletion fraction p
limitations: rooting depth is the midpoint of the printed range; actual depth is limited by hardpan, water table and tillage depth, none of which is known per field
p is the no-stress depletion fraction for a standard crop under standard management
rice p=0.20 describes a saturated root zone; it is not a model of flooded-paddy or alternate-wetting-and-drying management

evidence.title: FAO Irrigation Water Management Training Manual 1, section 2.4: available water content by soil type
limitations: retrieved 2026-09-10; the manual publishes available water content only (sand 25-100, loam 100-175, clay 175-250 mm/m)
a medium-textured loam is assumed for every field, because no per-field texture is collected anywhere in the product
field_capacity and wilting_point below are a texture-typical split whose DIFFERENCE equals the published loam midpoint of 137.5 mm/m; only that difference is sourced

total available water, which drives the soil water balance, depends only on the difference and is therefore sourced; the absolute field_capacity value is not, and it is used only on the rarer path where a same-day volumetric soil moisture reading exists
a confirmed soil observation for the field should supersede these values once soil texture is captured
